note: A claim is 'proven' only when an artefact exists that a third party can regenerate. Anything built and tested but not demonstrated end to end says 'pending' and names what it waits on.

claims.claim: A subject who cannot mobilise the threshold cannot obtain authorization.
claims.mechanism: The amount is measured on chain as a balance delta against a proof-bound snapshot and required to equal the threshold exactly. No calldata field asserts it.
claims.reproduce: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/run-campaign.ts  # 20 below-threshold cases, plus contract tests

claims.claim: A cleared challenge cannot be replayed.
claims.mechanism: Consumption is on chain and checked in both the proving and execution legs, so a replay never reaches mainnet or costs a pool fee.

claims.claim: A challenge cannot be redirected to another target or action.
claims.mechanism: The anonymizer calls only the bound target, on a fixed entry point. The target independently checks the caller is its own Limen deployment.

claims.claim: Another token cannot satisfy a token-specific challenge.
claims.mechanism: Snapshot and delta are taken on the challenge's token; the target checks the token independently.
Expiry is checked against the executing block, not the proving base, so a proof generated before expiry still fails if it lands after.

claims.claim: Direct calls cannot bypass the pool.
claims.mechanism: The clearing entry point accepts only the pinned pool, and no plain privacy_invoke exists on the anonymizer.

claims.claim: Only the bound subject can clear a subject-bound challenge.
claims.mechanism: The subject is the pool's identity key, derived inside the proof from the spender's private viewing key. It cannot be presented without that key.
claims.note: Both mainnet clearances used subject-bound challenges, not bearer.

claims.claim: Capital returns to shielded state in the same transaction, and a target revert strands nothing.
claims.mechanism: The pool credits the measured amount into an open note atomically; any revert aborts the whole transaction.

claims.claim: Whether a clearance was funded entirely from private notes is publicly verifiable per transaction.
claims.mechanism: An ERC-20 balance carries no provenance, so the contract cannot enforce the source. The pool publishes Withdrawal{to_addr,token,amount} in the same transaction, so Withdrawal.amount == threshold proves it. See DECISIONS.md D-007.
claims.note: Both mainnet clearances pass this check. It is a disclosed boundary made measurable, not a property the contract enforces.

claims.claim: The Limen self-hosted prover can produce a Mainnet-accepted STRK20 proof.
claims.mechanism: Limen runs the pinned upstream prover, rebuilt from the commit the published image names in its own labels, on its own host. All three clearances were proven there.
claims.note: 51.6s and 56.0s respectively. The published image could not run on this host at all (CONTRIBUTIONS.md C-1).

claims.claim: At least three qualifying Mainnet transactions touching the STRK20 pool exist.
claims.mechanism: Two Limen clearances plus the bootstrap private transfer, each re-read from chain and reconstructed from pool events.

claims.claim: Limen is built against the pool class actually deployed on mainnet.
claims.mechanism: The pinned upstream revision compiles to the class hash live at the pool. CI fails if that stops holding.

claims.claim: No privileged party can fabricate a clearance.
claims.mechanism: The anonymizer has no owner, no admin, no pause, no upgrade and no sweep. Creating a challenge authorises nothing.

claims.claim: Proving requests cannot leak viewing-key material into logs, metrics or errors.
claims.mechanism: Redaction at every emitting boundary, with tests asserting a viewing key cannot survive serialisation nested in calldata, inside errors, or past a depth bound.

claims.claim: Limen's self-hosted prover proves real STRK20 workloads reliably, and where it cannot the reason is stated.
claims.mechanism: Fourteen real mainnet transactions replayed against the block before inclusion. Failures are classified from the prover's own error text: two the sequencer refused at the proving base, two needing GetBlockHash which its virtual mode does not implement. All ten provable replays proved, p50 49.1 s, p95 57.7 s.

claims.claim: Every deterministic artefact in this repository regenerates from a fresh clone with no credentials.
claims.mechanism: scripts/clean-room.sh clones, asserts no secret survived the clone or the history, bootstraps, runs both suites, regenerates the campaign and requires a zero diff, and re-verifies the mainnet clearances from chain using only a public RPC.
